summary: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong (circa 2008–2013), studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti as well as teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima (born 1952) is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Toyama Chubu High School (1968–1971), he held academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (circa 1985–1997) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1997–2018).

Tsultrim Allione (born 1947) is a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Abo Rinpoche, Chögyam Trungpa, and Namkhai Norbu, and earned a master's degree from Antioch University by 1982. She also founded Tara Mandala.
Tsultrim Gyatso is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He has served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang and as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Tsultrim Kelsang (born 1939) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University from 1984 to 2002, was appointed a researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015, and held a post at the International Buddhist Association.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki (born 1943) is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tokyo University of Education (1962–1971), he served as a professor at Kyoto University (circa 1992–2006) and held a post at Doshisha University (circa 2006).

Tsuruji Sahoda (1899–1986) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. After studying at Kyoto University (1920–1923), he held academic posts at Ritsumeikan University (circa 1928–1950) and Osaka University (circa 1950–1962).
Tsutomu Hatai (1928–2018) was a scholar in Indology and other fields. Succeeding Hiroshi Maruyama, he served as president of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai from circa 1978 to 2018.
Tsutomu Horio (born 1949) is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. A student of Keiji Nishitani, he served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1996 to 2015.
Tsutomu Kubo (1883–1972) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1906–1909) and held a post at Tohoku University from circa 1923 to 1944.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Tsyben Zhamtsarano (1881–1942) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences in 1920.

Tu Weiming (born 1940) specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies, earning his PhD from Harvard. He held posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard (1981–2010), the Harvard-Yenching Institute as director (circa 1996–2008), and Peking University (circa 2010).
Tukaram Krishna Laddu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Tulku Sherdor (born 1961) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, learning under teachers Ted Norton, Jeffrey Hopkins, and traditional teacher Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Tulku Thondup (1939–2023) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Dodrupchen Monastery under teachers including Dodrupchen Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche, he was a visiting scholar at Harvard University (circa 1980–1983).

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (1920–1996) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught numerous students.

Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) was a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Washington and under Giuseppe Tucci. He served at the University of Washington from 1953 to 1957 as Associate Professor of Tibetan Language and Civilization.

Tyler Dewar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute (1997) and under traditional teachers Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Acharya Tashi Wangchuk, and Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen.

Tzungkuen Wen is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a PhD at the University of Queensland (2003–2009) under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang, and served as a lecturer at the Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005.
